en.title: Phasmophobia Dev Kinetic Games Launches Publishing Arm, Unveils Five New Titles
en.summary: The studio behind the hit ghost-hunting phenomenon **Phasmophobia** is expanding its horizons. Kinetic Games has officially announced the launch of its own publishing label, Kinetic Publishing, and revealed an impressive initial slate of five diverse games.
en.body:
From the terror-filled halls of **Phasmophobia** to the wider world of game development, **Kinetic Games** is making a bold move. The studio, which found massive success with its cooperative ghost-hunting simulator, has officially launched **Kinetic Publishing**. This new venture aims to support and elevate independent game developers, a mission spearheaded by **Daniel Knight**, CEO of Kinetic Games. "It’s such an exciting time for indie game development," Knight stated, reflecting on the company's growth. "The fact we’ve grown so much as a company means we’re now in the place where we want to support studios who come under our wing, and provide the support I'd have appreciated at the start of my journey."

Kinetic Publishing's inaugural lineup promises something for every type of player, showcasing a commitment to diverse genres and innovative experiences. Leading the charge is **Precognition**, a new narrative-driven title from **Half Mermaid**, the acclaimed studio behind **Immortality**, **Her Story**, and **Telling Lies**. Co-developed with filmmaker **Brandon Cronenberg**, **Precognition** will leverage Half Mermaid's signature blend of full-motion video and interactive storytelling, putting players in the shoes of Diana, who can see the future after a mysterious brain implant. This collaboration alone signals a high level of ambition for the new label.

Beyond the star power of Half Mermaid, the publishing slate includes a variety of intriguing projects. Players can anticipate a punky racing game featuring witches on broomsticks, a tense, **Papers, Please**-esque experience set in space, and a cozy, **Spiritfarer**-inspired title. Rounding out the announced games is a metroidvania that reportedly introduces a novel mechanic, even differentiating itself from critically lauded titles like **Hollow Knight**. While specific details on all these titles are still emerging, the curated selection highlights a keen eye for unique concepts and passionate development teams.

## A New Era for Indie Support
The launch of Kinetic Publishing is more than just an expansion for Kinetic Games; it represents a significant step in supporting the indie development scene. With **Phasmophobia** having achieved global recognition and commercial success, the studio is now in a position to offer resources and a platform to other creators. This initiative is particularly meaningful given the challenges faced by independent studios in securing funding and visibility. By leveraging their own hard-won experience, Kinetic Games aims to foster an environment where creativity can flourish, potentially leading to the next generation of breakout indie hits.

## What's Next
Kinetic Publishing is set to officially reveal more about its upcoming slate at a new indie gaming showcase scheduled for August. This event, hosted by **Ben Starr**, will offer a deeper dive into the five announced games and may hint at future projects. While Kinetic Games will continue its dedicated focus on **Phasmophobia**, its new publishing arm is poised to make a substantial impact on the gaming landscape in the coming years, with the first titles expected to launch in 2027 and 2028.

content_raw: Kinetic Games is expanding into the games publishing business. Before today, Kinetic has only been known for Phasmophobia , its four-player ghost-hunting game that first exploded during the COVID pandemic and has remained a favorite since then. It has apparently done well enough to allow the team to expand its business into publishing, as it's announced a group of five games that make up its initial publishing efforts. The lineup includes one horror title--and man, is it a big one--and also features other kinds of games, including a punky racing game starring witches on broomsticks, a super-tense Papers, Please-like experience in space, a cozy game inspired by Spiritfarer, and a metroidvania game that does something even Hollow Knight didn't think of. Here's what's coming from Kinetic Publishing. Precognition Developed by Half Mermaid In terms of name recognition, Sam Barlow's team at Half Mermaid is the biggest one attached to the new label. Project C, Half Mermaid's previously announced working-title project with Brandon Cronenberg (of the Cronenberg body-horror film dynasty), has officially been revealed as Precognition.  The team behind Immortality, Her Story, and Telling Lies is back again with another blend of full-motion-video gameplay, non-linear storytelling, and a deep rabbit hole for players to fall into. In Precognition, you'll play as Diana, who discovers she can see the future after receiving an experimental brain implant. As players explore these visions, they'll commit some to Diana's memory based on choices they make. In turn, they will alter the course of the story, which is being co-developed with Cronenberg. All three of Barlow's games to date have earned widespread acclaim, so suffice it to say this is a big get for Kinetic.  Precognition is coming to PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2 in Spring 2028. Precognition on Steam Aether Wizard Life Developed by Vonder Games Fans of cozy games such as Spiritfarer and Stardew Valley will want to keep an eye on Aether Wizard Life from Vonder Games. In it, you'll create your own mage and live out your life in a customizable castle that resembles Spiritfarer's boat-building tools very closely. You can tend to animals, cook meals, grow crops, and work jobs around different towns. All the while, you'll be exploring a story with a touch of darkness to it, as a secret organization is endangering the lives of mages all over, and you'll need to get to the bottom of the situation. Aether will feature romanceable characters, a wide variety of activities to perform outside of story missions, and 30+ skills to learn and master.  As someone who loves Spiritfarer so much that I got a tattoo commemorating it, I'm really looking forward to this one. While the home-building tools are familiar, a lot else stands apart, so it's an enticing combination of what I've seen before next to new experiences. Aether Wizard Life is due out in Fall 2028 on PC, PS5, Xbox Series
